_comment: Pinned upstream digests for the Aether core (PROMPT.md PHASE 6).
The release archives and their .sha256 companions live at the same base URL, so
verifying an archive against the checksum file beside it proves only that the transfer
was intact - anyone able to replace the release can replace both. These values are
committed here so the expected digest comes from this repository at review time rather
than from the server being verified.
Provenance, recorded in security-evidence/logs/upstream-provenance.txt: 'archives' are
the asset digests GitHub itself reports through the releases API for tag v1.9.0
(published 2026-09-04T17:17:48Z), which is a different source from the release's own
.sha256 files. 'binary' is the SHA-256 of the executable extracted from the archive.
For the Windows zip that value is what src-tauri/src/process.rs pins as AETHER_SHA256 and
refuses to launch without, and it has been verified against the bytes on disk. The three
Android values were established the same way and are not independent of 'archives': each
was obtained by extracting an archive whose digest had already matched the API-sourced pin
above, so it inherits that archive's trust rather than asserting anything new. They are
recorded so the .so actually copied into the APK can be checked at build time without a
second download, and so the shipped native payload has a reviewable expected digest at all
- android/app/src/main/jniLibs/**/*.so is .gitignore'd, so before this it had none.
Verified 2026-09-02: all three shipped jniLibs .so files are byte-identical to the binary
inside the matching pinned archive (security-evidence/logs/phase6-android-native.txt).
Both platforms are now on v1.9.0. Windows moved from v1.8.0 to v1.9.0 on 2026-09-10 so
the warp-in-warp endpoints the GUI caches can be handed back to the core through
AETHER_WIW_PEERS, which v1.8.0 has no equivalent for; the Windows digests below were
re-derived from a fresh download and cross-checked against the releases API on that date.
'androidVersion' and its separate digest maps are kept because scripts/
fetch-android-assets.ps1 reads them, and because they let one platform move ahead of the
other again without disturbing the payload of the one that stays. While the two versions
agree, the android* maps below duplicate the Android entries in 'archives' and 'binary';
if they ever disagree, the android* maps are the authority for Android.
Updating either core means changing its version and every digest in one reviewed commit.
Building against any other version requires the caller to supply the digest
explicitly via AETHER_EXPECTED_SHA256; the fetch scripts will not fall back to the
server's own checksum file.
This is data rather than a .ps1 so it needs no execution policy to read and can be
consumed by the release manifest and SBOM tooling as well as by the fetch scripts.
Built from source rather than downloaded, so there is no upstream archive digest to pin.
The trust anchor is the commit: fetch-android-assets.ps1 clones the tag, then refuses to
continue unless HEAD is exactly this commit, and checks submodule state. The resulting
.so digests are recorded as observed output of that build on the release host - they are
NOT an independent pin, because an ndk-build output depends on the NDK and host, and this
project has not established that the build is bit-reproducible. Treat a mismatch as a
signal to re-derive, not as proof of tampering.
